claim: Three views of the control machinery. A catalogue identifies controls; an interaction graph relates controls through shared resources and exposes potential conflicts; and a coverage view relates controls to independently identified engineering obligations. The same control identities appear across all three views. Coverage analysis can reveal obligations lacking adequate controls (coverage gaps) and controls lacking a current justification (candidate orphans).
topology: Control machinery feeds all three views. Engineering obligations feed only coverage. In the interaction graph the squash rule and diff-size guard point to the same commit set. Coverage connects atomic delivery to A and bounded change scope to B. Neither unmatched example has an edge.
bw_encoding: Gray headers identify the three views. Dashed outlines mark the unmatched cost ceiling and legacy export check.
redesign: Compare the machinery with independently identified obligations to find missing coverage and controls needing justification. Shared access to a resource identifies potential interactions.
alt: Control machinery supplies the catalogue, interaction graph, and coverage view. Independently identified obligations also feed coverage. The squash rule and diff-size guard share the commit set. Atomic delivery traces to the squash rule, bounded change scope to the diff-size guard. A cost ceiling lacks coverage, and a legacy export check lacks a recorded justification.
